drafts.title: $4.30 a gallon in Colorado today. Here's my cost per mile. (MAIN, Fri 12-1 PM today)
drafts.ocr_why: Dollar opener, his own number, and a question every driver can answer in one line.
drafts.window: Fri ~12-1 PM MT today (Friday's bright noon cell). Don't run the 38,000-mile post the same day.
drafts.angle: Simple per-mile receipt: what gas drivers pay per mile this morning next to what his Model Y costs charging at home. Not a used-price or lease post.
bullets: AAA Oct 30: Colorado regular $4.3049; national $4.2046.
A year ago the national average was $3.0377, about $1.17 a gallon less than today.
AAA says crude above $100 a barrel is keeping prices from dropping further.
A 25 mpg car at $4.30 is about 17 cents a mile (our math, example mpg).
drafts.body:
"$4.30 a gallon in Colorado this morning.

I did the math for a regular 25 mpg car. That's about 17 cents every mile you drive. A year ago the national average was about a dollar seventeen cheaper.

My Model Y charging in the garage here in Grand Junction: [___ cents a mile at ___ cents per kWh]. [photo: app charge stats or the home charging screen]

I'm not trying to sell anybody a car. I spent years behind a parts counter watching people pour money into gas and repairs, and the per-mile number is the one nobody looks at.

What's your cost per mile right now? Gas or electric, I want the real number."
drafts.pixel: At a gas station sign or in the garage plugging in, 10 seconds, his face: "$4.30 out there. Here's what mine costs."
drafts.target: Quote @SawyerMerritt or another big verified EV account when they post today's AAA gas numbers, with his cents-per-mile line.

drafts.title: $2,875 back from Xcel on one Powerwall 3: my battery quotes (Sun ~noon if quotes are in, else Tue ~noon)
drafts.ocr: Strong once he has real quote numbers; Weak with blanks
drafts.ocr_why: Real shopper with real dollars, a follow-up to the question he already asked, and every Colorado solar owner can weigh in.
drafts.window: Sun ~12 PM MT if quotes are in hand; otherwise Tue ~12 PM MT.
drafts.angle: He already asked "Powerwall or Enphase?" publicly. This is the receipt once quotes come in: what Colorado actually pays you back, in plain dollars. Don't re-ask the question.
bullets: Xcel Colorado Renewable Battery Connect: $250 per kW, which Tesla says is $2,875 per Powerwall 3, capped at $5,000 per customer.
Plus a $100 a year bill credit for 5 years; Xcel can draw on the battery during grid events.
Runs through 2027 or until funds run out; check arrives within about 60 days of permission to operate. Enphase IQ batteries qualify at the same $250 per kW.
Typical installed with solar (HomeElectrified 2026 guide): Powerwall 3 about $15,000 for 13.5 kWh; Enphase IQ 10C about $14,250 for 10 kWh.
Enphase warranty 15 years vs Tesla 10. No federal tax credit for home batteries in 2026.
drafts.body:
"$2,875. That's what Xcel pays back on one Powerwall 3 here in Colorado. Plus $100 a year off my bill for five years.

I asked earlier which battery you'd pick. Now I've got actual quotes.

Tesla: [$___]
Enphase: [$___]

The catch: Xcel gets to pull from the battery during grid emergencies, and the program ends when the money runs out. There's no federal tax credit on batteries this year, so the Xcel check matters.

I'm leaning [___] because [___]. My Enphase panels have been [___] so far.

If you added a battery, what tipped it for you? Price, warranty, or the brand you already had?"
drafts.pixel: Standing at the garage wall where a battery would go, 20 seconds: "Here's where it goes. Here's what each one costs me after Xcel's check."
drafts.target: Quote @TeslaEnergy or @Enphase (both on his watch list) with the Colorado rebate line.

drafts.title: What does a mile actually cost?
drafts.body:
A gas price sign only tells half the story.

At an example $4 a gallon and 25 mpg, fuel costs 16 cents a mile.

For an EV, compare electricity bought with miles driven, including charging losses.

Use your own prices. What does a mile actually cost you?
bullets: Illustrative arithmetic: $4 divided by 25 miles per gallon is $0.16 per mile. This is not a claim about current Colorado prices or Brian's car.
DOE explains EV fuel cost using electricity price and energy use per mile. Metered charging electricity includes charging losses. This compares energy costs only, not total ownership costs.

drafts.title: Start a battery quote with the fridge
drafts.body:
Shopping for a home battery? Start with the fridge, lights and anything else you need during an outage.

Ask the installer: which circuits will work, and for how long?

Battery size alone does not answer that. What would your household need to keep running?
bullets: California Air Resources Board explains that backup systems must meet both power demand and stored-energy needs for sufficient runtime.
This is a shopping checklist, not a product recommendation, rebate claim or guaranteed runtime. Circuit coverage and runtime require a home-specific installer assessment.

drafts.title: Start with something you already enjoy
drafts.body:
Helping someone try AI for the first time? Start with a hobby they already enjoy.

Try: "Explain three photography terms in plain English, with an example of each."

Check the answers together. No personal documents needed.

What would your first question be?
bullets: An original suggested learning exercise, not a claim about a particular AI product or personal experience.

NIST identifies validity, reliability and privacy as AI trustworthiness considerations. The advice to check answers and avoid personal documents applies those principles; NIST does not prescribe this photography prompt.
